title: perf(ai): run_sql seeks trace-id lookups through trace_index and stops at the row cap

summaries.body:
## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 8/10** · likely safe to merge Held at 8 because a warning is open. 1 warning −1 · tests covered · risk medium · 1/1 new units observable `run_sql` now ANDs a `trace_index` seek onto unbounded literal trace-id lookups (with a fallback to the query as written) and returns 1,000 rows at the cap instead of failing. The rewrite is well guarded; the new cap flag misfires on results of exactly 1,000 rows. - `withTraceIndexSeek` ANDs a `trace_index` tuple seek onto literal `TraceId` predicates - `run_sql` reruns the query as written when the seeked form is invalid SQL - `prepareRawSql({ truncateAtCap })` emits `LIMIT 1000` and the tool returns those rows - `RunSqlOutput.atRowCap` reports the cap instead of the hard failure ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F1 · atRowCap fires on results of exactly 1,000 rows that were not cut correctness · [`apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/run-sql.ts:411`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/0c3d53679e99492911273d72b9a93d2a32089000/apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/run-sql.ts#L411) `prepareRawSql` now emits `LIMIT 1000` for `run_sql` (packages/query-engine/src/runtime/raw-sql.ts:158), which drops the extra row that used to be the overflow sentinel (`RAW_SQL_FETCH_ROW_LIMIT = MAX_RAW_SQL_RESULT_ROWS + 1`, "one extra row is the overflow sentinel for the public 1,000-row cap"). With the sentinel gone, `rowCount >= MAX_RAW_SQL_RESULT_ROWS` cannot tell a truncated result from one that happened to return exactly 1,000 rows, so those queries get the "Stopped at the 1000-row cap, so more rows may exist" notice and a false `atRowCap` in `structuredContent`, and the agent spends a round trip re-aggregating. ``` Keep the sentinel: have `prepareRawSql` keep `RAW_SQL_FETCH_ROW_LIMIT` when `truncateAtCap` is set, skip only the rows branch of `rawSqlResultLimitError` in that case, and truncate `rows` to `MAX_RAW_SQL_RESULT_ROWS` here so `atRowCap` can be `rowCount > MAX_RAW_SQL_RESULT_ROWS`. ```
What was checked - Seeked SQL still passes `rawSqlIssue`: the added subquery's `$__orgFilter` sits after a `WHERE`, so `orgFilterEscapes` returns false (`raw-sql.ts:511`) - Protocol cap uses `rows > maxRows`, so 1,000 rows pass `maxRows: 1000` (`lib/effect-clickhouse-http/src/protocol.ts:99`) - Skip rules verified against `definedNames` (only `AS x` aliases) and `referencedTableNames` (one entry per catalog table)
Observability coverage: 1 of 1 changes observable | Change | Kind | Observable | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | run_sql trace-id seek and fallback rerun | warehouse query path | yes | Both statements go through `runRawSql` → `WarehouseQueryService.rawSqlQuery` with `context: "mcp.run_sql"` (apps/ai/src/mcp/lib/run-raw-sql.ts:65), under the dispatcher's `maple.mcp.tool` span |

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 9/10** · safe to merge The seek is a provable narrowing of the predicate and the row cap keeps the result limits; one edge case over the length gate and one untested wiring remain. 2 notes · tests partial −1 · risk medium · 1/1 new units observable `run_sql` now seeks unbounded `TraceId` lookups through `trace_index` and returns 1,000 rows with an `atRowCap` notice instead of failing. The rewrite can only narrow what the predicate already selects, so it is safe to merge. - `withTraceIndexSeek` ANDs a `trace_index` seek onto unbounded `TraceId` predicates - `prepareRawSql` emits `LIMIT 1000` for `run_sql` through `truncateAtCap` - `run_sql` reports `atRowCap` instead of failing past 1,000 rows ### Findings
🔵 Note · F2 · Seek pushes a near-limit statement past MAX_RAW_SQL_LENGTH correctness · [`apps/ai/src/mcp/lib/trace-seek.ts:56-57`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/32224d90bb957eb0c08329b669ef91ac36b94e3f/apps/ai/src/mcp/lib/trace-seek.ts#L56-L57) `rawSqlIssue` rejects any statement longer than 32,768 characters (`packages/domain/src/raw-sql.ts:633`), and this file gates on the original SQL (line 36) before the ~180-character seek is appended. A statement already within 180 characters of the limit passes the gate, then the seeked form fails with `RawSqlValidationError`, which `run-sql.ts:370` does not fall back on, so the agent is told its own valid SQL is too long. ``` Capture the `reduceRight` result, `return seeked.length > MAX_RAW_SQL_LENGTH ? undefined : seeked`, and import `MAX_RAW_SQL_LENGTH` from `@maple/domain/raw-sql`. ```
🔵 Note · F3 · Seek-fallback test passes whether or not the seek is issued tests · [`apps/ai/src/mcp/__evals__/run-sql-recovery.test.ts:137`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/32224d90bb957eb0c08329b669ef91ac36b94e3f/apps/ai/src/mcp/__evals__/run-sql-recovery.test.ts#L137) The fallback rule and the plain rule both match the same statement (`sql.includes(FALLBACK_ID)`), and the assertions only read the final `rows`, so the test stays green when `withTraceIndexSeek` is removed from `run-sql.ts:364` — the headline rewrite would disappear with every test passing. Record every issued statement in the fake (as the `product_events` rule does) and assert the first one carried `FROM trace_index`.
What was checked - Seek tuple is byte-identical to the production `inTraces` reader (`packages/query-engine/src/ch/tables.ts:142`) - `trace_index`'s MV has no row filter, so the seek stays a subset of the `TraceId` rows (`materializations.ts:1160`) - `truncateAtCap` results still pass the 1,000-row and 5 MB caps (`runtime/raw-sql.ts:163`); `atRowCap` fires only at exactly 1,000

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 8/10** · likely safe to merge Held at 8 because a warning is open. 1 warning −1 · tests covered · risk medium · 1/1 new units observable Adds a trace_index seek to the tool's SQL when a trace-id filter has no time bound, and replaces the run_sql row-limit error with a capped result marked `atRowCap`. The seek logic is guarded and tested; one row-count edge case needs fixing before merge. - `withTraceIndexSeek` ANDs a `trace_index` seek onto literal `TraceId` predicates in unbounded `traces` queries - `run_sql` wraps the statement in `LIMIT 1000` and returns rows with `atRowCap` instead of failing - A seeked statement the warehouse cannot analyse is re-run as written on `WarehouseInvalidSQL` ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F4 · limitedWithinCap reads the offset of LIMIT offset, count as the row count correctness · [`apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/run-sql.ts:296-301`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/33c8ed1dacb23ac7a909597ad9c9cf242b7b973b/apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/run-sql.ts#L296-L301) In ClickHouse's `LIMIT offset, count` form the count is the second number, but `OWN_LIMIT` captures the first, so `SELECT ... LIMIT 5, 5000` yields `own[1] = 5` and `limitedWithinCap` returns true. The result is then exactly 1,000 rows (`atRowCap` suppressed) and the model is told the truncated answer is complete — the failure this PR set out to remove. `LIMIT 2000, 1000` fails the other way: 1,000 rows with nothing cut, and a spurious cap notice. ``` const OWN_LIMIT = /\bLIMIT\s+(?:(\d+)\s*,\s*(\d+)|(\d+)(?:\s+OFFSET\s+\d+)?)\s*;?\s*$/i /** The statement ends in its own LIMIT of at most the cap, so a full page is its answer, not ours. */ const limitedWithinCap = (sql: string): boolean => { const own = OWN_LIMIT.exec(maskLiteralsAndComments(sql).trimEnd()) const count = own === null ? undefined : Number(own[2] ?? own[3]) return count !== undefined && count <= MAX_RAW_SQL_RESULT_ROWS } ```
What was checked - `maskLiteralsAndComments` preserves offsets (raw-sql.ts:637), so the new splice-by-index logic lands on the right characters - `trace_index` sort key `(OrgId, TraceId, ServiceName, Bucket)` serves the seek's `TraceId IN (...)` lookup, and `traces` is keyed on `(OrgId, ServiceName, bucket, TraceId)` - `rawSqlResultLimitError` rejects only `>` the cap, so a truncated 1,000-row result passes; the seeked statement with a second `$__orgFilter` inside the subquery is issued by the eval test

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 10/10** · safe to merge Seek rewriting is guarded and every skip rule plus the row cap is pinned by tests; only the cap notice is heuristic, and the gain on large tenants is unmeasured. 1 note · tests covered · risk medium · 1/1 new units observable Rewrites `run_sql`'s unbounded trace-id lookups to seek through `trace_index` and turns the 1,000-row hard failure into a truncated result with an `atRowCap` notice. The rewrite is conjunct-ANDed and conservative; safe to merge. - `withTraceIndexSeek` ANDs a `trace_index` seek onto unbounded literal `TraceId` lookups - `run_sql` re-runs the SQL as written when the seeked form fails as invalid SQL - `truncateAtCap` wraps `run_sql` in `LIMIT 1000` and sets `atRowCap` ### Findings
🔵 Note · F5 · limitedWithinCap reads a subquery LIMIT as the statement's own cap correctness · [`apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/run-sql.ts:300-302`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/73e4b6b979d9b1faf5b6e4cef947eb37fe831953/apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/run-sql.ts#L300-L302) `OWN_LIMIT` only matches a `LIMIT` at the very end of the statement, so it also reports `false` whenever the count came from a limit the trailing-clause check cannot see. `SELECT * FROM (SELECT number FROM logs WHERE $__orgFilter ORDER BY Timestamp DESC LIMIT 1000)` returns exactly 1,000 rows from its own inner `LIMIT` and still gets `atRowCap: true`, telling the agent more rows may exist and to add a `LIMIT` it already wrote. ``` Base the notice on the criteria that the result was actually cut, not on the shape of the statement's tail — e.g. keep the 1,001st overflow row for `run_sql` (fetch `RAW_SQL_FETCH_ROW_LIMIT`, drop the extra row, set `atRowCap` from its presence) and keep the `LIMIT 1000` wrapper for the rows returned. ```
What was checked - `trace_index` covers every span: `trace_index_mv` groups all of `traces` unfiltered, both 30-day TTLs - The seeked SQL still passes `rawSqlIssue`: `FROM trace_index` is unrestricted and `$__orgFilter` expands globally - `LIMIT 1000` stays under the row check, which fails only above it (`query-engine/src/runtime/raw-sql.ts:164`)
